funFact: A real lion's roar can be heard five miles away — that's like roaring across a whole town!
story: Leo the little lion was too shy to roar. One morning he took the biggest breath of his life, and his roar shook the mango trees — the whole jungle cheered!
description: Kneel down and sit on your heels, brave lion! 🦁 Put your paws on your knees and take a giiiant sniff of air. Now open your mouth wide, stick out your tongue, and ROAR it all out! Do it again — even louder!

funFact: Cobras can lift a third of their body straight up off the ground — just like this pose!
story: In a sunny sandpit lived Coco the cobra, who loved to rise up tall every morning to say hissss-hello to the sun.
description: Lie on your tummy, sneaky cobra! 🐍 Put your hands flat under your shoulders. Press down gently and lift your chest up, keeping your hips on the floor. Look forward and give your best hisssssss!

funFact: Frogs don't drink water with their mouths — they soak it up through their skin!
story: Fernanda the frog found the perfect lily pad. She folded up small and quiet, waiting for a friendly dragonfly to float by.
description: Kneel down, little frog, and slide your knees out wide. 🐸 Sit back toward your heels and fold forward, resting your arms on the floor. Take a slow froggy breath... and whisper a tiny ribbit!

funFact: Eagles can spot a rabbit from two miles up in the sky — super vision!
story: Ellie the eaglet wrapped her wings tight, took a steady breath, and got ready for her very first flight off the mountain.
description: Stand tall, little eagle! 🦅 Cross one leg over the other and give yourself a big wing hug by crossing your arms too. Bend your knees a tiny bit and balance like you're perched on a cliff. Wobbling is part of the fun — eagles ride the wind!

funFact: A camel's humps don't hold water — they store energy snacks made of fat!
story: Cleo the camel carried her friends across the sunny desert, then stretched her chest to the sky to celebrate the journey.
description: Kneel up nice and tall, desert friend! 🐫 Put your hands on your lower back like pockets. Lift your chest to the sky and lean back just a little — you're a proud camel! Come up slowly when you're done.

funFact: Some fish sleep with their eyes open because they don't have eyelids!
story: Finn the fish loved to float on his back at the top of the pond, puffing his shiny chest at the sun.
description: Lie on your back, splashy fish! 🐟 Slide your hands under your hips, press your elbows down, and lift your chest up like a wave. Let the back of your head rest lightly on the floor. Blub blub — breathe big fishy breaths!

funFact: A peacock's tail can have more than 150 shimmering feathers, and each one has an eye spot!
story: Percy the peacock practiced every day until he could lift his glorious tail feather high — and the whole garden went ooooh!
description: Stand tall, fancy peacock! 🦚 Reach back and hold one ankle behind you. Stretch your other arm up like a shining feather and lean forward just a little bit. Balance and show off your beautiful tail!
safetyNote: Practice near a wall or with a grown-up close by for balance.

funFact: Cats spend most of the day stretching and napping — they're natural yogis!
story: Milo the kitten woke from a nap in the sunbeam, arched his back way up high, and purred his happiest purr.
description: Come to your hands and knees, cozy kitty! 🐱 Breathe out and round your back way up to the ceiling, tucking your chin. Make the roundest cat back you can... and purr! Meowvelous!

funFact: Cows have best friends in their herd and get happier when they're together!
story: Clover the cow lifted her head to smell the morning meadow, let her belly sway low, and gave the sweetest moo.
description: Stay on your hands and knees, friendly cow! 🐮 Breathe in, let your belly sink down low, and lift your head and tail to the sky. Now give me your biggest MOOOO! Try switching between cat and cow — it feels amazing.

funFact: Real dogs do this exact stretch when they wake up — that's why it's called Downward Dog!
story: Biscuit the puppy woke up from a nap, stretched his paws way out front, wiggled his tail high, and was ready to play fetch!
description: Start on your hands and knees, wiggly puppy! 🐶 Tuck your toes and lift your tail-bone way up high to make a mountain shape. Press your paws into the floor and let your head hang happy. Can you wag your tail up there? Woof woof!

funFact: Pigeons are amazing navigators — they can find their way home from hundreds of miles away!
story: Pip the pigeon flew all the way across the city, then tucked one leg under her fluffy chest for a cozy rooftop rest.
description: From hands and knees, slide one knee up behind your wrist, little pigeon. 🕊️ Stretch your other leg long behind you. Now fold forward over your front leg and rest like a sleepy bird. Coo-coo... switch sides when you're ready!

funFact: Butterflies taste their food with their feet — imagine tasting ice cream with your toes!
story: Bella the butterfly landed on a daisy, fluttered her brand-new wings in the sunshine, and felt light as a giggle.
description: Sit up tall and press the bottoms of your feet together, beautiful butterfly! 🦋 Hold your feet like a little cocoon. Now flutter your knee-wings up and down, slow then fast! Finish with soft, slow flutters and a big smile.

funFact: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton — it can feel you pat it!
story: Tilly the turtle heard the rain start, so she tucked into her cozy shell and listened to the drip-drop lullaby.
description: Sit with your legs wide and knees soft, slow-and-steady turtle. 🐢 Slide your arms under your knees and fold forward into your shell. Get quiet and small... peek out when the sun comes back!

funFact: Crows are so clever they can use sticks as tools and even recognize friendly faces!
story: Kiki the baby crow put her feet on a branch, leaned onto her strong wings, and lifted one toe at a time — she was almost flying!
description: Squat down low and plant your hands flat like strong roots, clever crow! 🐦‍⬛ Snuggle your knees onto the backs of your arms. Lean forward sloooowly and let one tiptoe get light, then the other. Even one tiny toe-lift makes you a flying crow — caw caw!
safetyNote: Put a pillow in front of you and keep a grown-up nearby. Lean forward only a little at a time.

funFact: A rabbit's big ears can turn almost all the way around to catch tiny sounds!
story: Rosie the rabbit hopped into her burrow at bedtime, curled up round and warm, and dreamed of clover fields.
description: Kneel down and sit on your heels, little bunny. 🐰 Fold forward until your forehead rests near the floor. Reach your paws back toward your feet and curl up round like a fluffy bunny in a burrow. Shhh... soft bunny breaths.

funFact: Baby deer can stand up and walk when they are only half an hour old!
story: Dara the deer stepped softly into a quiet clearing, folded her legs neatly beneath her, and listened to the forest hum.
description: Sit on the floor, graceful deer. 🦌 Bend one leg in front of you and sweep the other leg back behind you, like folded deer legs. Sit up tall and proud, then turn gently to look over the meadow. Switch sides, soft and slow.

funFact: Swans can sleep while floating on the water, drifting like feathery boats!
story: Snow the swan glided across the glassy lake, lifted her long neck to the moon, and the whole pond went hush.
description: Slide one leg forward and bend it, stretching the other leg long behind you, elegant swan. 🦢 Press your hands down and lift your chest up tall. Stretch your swan neck looong to the sky. Glide to the other side when you're ready!

funFact: Herons can stand perfectly still for many minutes waiting for a fish — champion statues!
story: Henry the heron stood at the edge of the silver river, lifted one long leg high, and stayed still as a statue until — splash!
description: Sit tall with one leg folded back beside you, patient heron. 🦩 Hold your other foot or shin with both hands. Now streeetch that leg up toward the sky, as straight as feels good. Sit tall and still like you're fishing... then switch legs!
safetyNote: Keep a small bend in your knee if the stretch feels too big. Never pull hard on your leg.

funFact: Fireflies make their glow with almost no heat — the most magical night-light in nature!
story: Sparkle the firefly practiced her take-off every evening, lifting her tiny toes off the leaf until — flash! — she lit up the whole garden.
description: Sit down and plant your hands flat beside your hips, glowing firefly! 🪲 Press down strong, squeeze your tummy, and see if your feet get light — even lifting your heels counts! Flash your brightest smile each time you lift. Blink, blink, glow!
safetyNote: Practice on a soft mat and keep lifts tiny. A grown-up spotter makes it extra fun.

funFact: Dolphins sleep with one half of their brain awake so they remember to swim up for air!
story: Splash the dolphin loved diving down deep and popping back up with a happy click-click-whistle for her pod.
description: Come to your knees and put your forearms flat on the floor, splashy dolphin! 🐬 Tuck your toes and lift your hips up high like a wave. Press your arms down strong and let your head hang free. Eee-eee! You're diving through the sea!

funFact: Grasshoppers can jump twenty times the length of their own body — like you jumping over a bus!
story: Greta the grasshopper crouched low in the tall grass, powered up her spring-legs, and got ready for her record-breaking leap.
description: Lie on your tummy with your arms by your sides, springy grasshopper! 🦗 Breathe in and lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor all at once. Hold your hop in mid-air — you're flying over the meadow! Land gently and try again.

funFact: A T-Rex's arms were tiny, but its bite was stronger than any land animal ever!
story: Rex the dinosaur stomped through the fern forest with his tiny arms tucked in, roaring hello to every dino he met.
description: Stand with your feet wide and bend your knees, mighty T-Rex! 🦖 Tuck your elbows in tight to make teeny-tiny dino arms. Take three slow, giant stomps in place — BOOM, BOOM, BOOM! Now freeze and give your loudest dino ROAR!

funFact: Foxes use their fluffy tails like blankets to keep warm while they sleep!
story: Fiona the fox tiptoed through the snowy woods so quietly that even the owls didn't hear her sneak by.
description: Crouch down low on your tiptoes, sneaky fox! 🦊 Make soft paw-hands in front of you and take three sloooow tiptoe steps. Now freeze and prick up your fox ears — what do you hear? Shhh... you're the quietest fox in the forest!

funFact: Sloths move so slowly that tiny green algae grows on their fur like a mossy sweater!
story: Stanley the sloth took one whole minute to reach the next branch, smiled his slow sloth smile, and decided it was nap o'clock.
description: Lie on your back and hug your knees sloooowly, sleepy sloth. 🦥 Rock gently side to side like you're swaying on a branch. Move as slowly as you possibly can... slower... slooower. Now melt into the floor for a mini sloth nap. Zzzz.

funFact: Penguins can't fly in the sky, but they fly underwater at up to twenty miles per hour!
story: Pebble the penguin waddled across the ice to bring his best friend a shiny stone — the penguin way of saying you're my pal.
description: Stand with your heels together and toes out, dapper penguin! 🐧 Keep your arms straight down like flippers. Waddle-waddle-waddle in tiny steps... and FREEZE like the ice! Hold super still, then waddle again. Brrr-illiant!

funFact: Kangaroos can't hop backwards — they only bounce forward, just like brave hearts!
story: Joey the kangaroo bounced across the sunny outback, then held super still so the emus couldn't find him in hide-and-seek.
description: Bend your knees and hold your paws up by your chest, bouncy kangaroo! 🦘 Do three springy hops forward, landing soft as a whisper. Now sink into a low kangaroo squat and HOLD it, strong and still. Feel those powerful roo legs!

funFact: Flamingos are born gray and fluffy — they turn pink from the shrimpy snacks they eat!
story: Frankie the flamingo stood on one leg in the warm lagoon all afternoon, feeling perfectly pink and perfectly proud.
description: Stand tall on one leg, fabulous flamingo! 🦩 Bend your other knee and lift that foot up behind you. Stretch your wings out wide for balance. If you wobble, that's just the breeze on the lagoon — try the other leg next!

funFact: Elephants can hear each other's rumbly stomps through the ground from miles away!
story: Ella the elephant led the parade to the watering hole, swinging her trunk and stomping a happy drumbeat for everyone to follow.
description: Stand with your feet wide, mighty elephant! 🐘 Clasp your hands together and let your arms swing low like a long trunk. Stomp one foot, then the other — BOOM, BOOM! Now swing your trunk way up high and trumpet: bah-rooooo!

funFact: A giraffe's neck is taller than a grown-up, but it has the same number of neck bones as yours — seven!
story: Gigi the giraffe spotted the juiciest leaf at the very top of the tallest tree, so she stretched and streeetched until she reached it.
description: Stand tall and reach both arms way up high, lovely giraffe! 🦒 Now rise up onto your tiptoes and stretch your neck looong toward the tastiest leaf. Hold it, wobble and all! Come down softly and munch, munch, munch.

funFact: Some monkeys have tails so strong they can hang from a branch using only their tail!
story: Momo the monkey dangled from the jungle gym, swinging gently and giggling at the upside-down world.
description: Stand with your feet apart and bend your knees a little, cheeky monkey! 🐒 Fold forward and let your arms dangle down like long monkey arms. Sway them side to side — ooh ooh ah ah! Roll up slowly, one bumpy bit of your back at a time.

funFact: Pandas do real somersaults down grassy hills just for fun!
story: Ping the panda finished her bamboo breakfast, tucked into a fuzzy ball, and rolled down the hill giggling all the way.
description: Sit down and hug your knees in tight, roly-poly panda! 🐼 Tuck your chin and rock gently back onto your back... and up again! Rock three times, then hold your panda ball nice and still. Squeeze that bamboo hug!

funFact: Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around because they have twice as many neck bones as you!
story: Olive the owl sat on her moonlit branch, slowly turning her head this way and that, keeping watch over the sleepy forest.
description: Sit criss-cross and tall like a wise owl on a branch. 🦉 Slooowly turn your head to one side as far as feels comfy — whooo's over there? Come back to the middle, then turn the other way. Finish with a soft owl hoot: whoo, whoo!

funFact: Snakes smell with their tongues — every flick tells them what's nearby!
story: Sami the snake slithered through the soft grass, wiggling left and right, following the smell of sunshine.
description: Lie on your tummy with your arms by your sides, wiggly snake! 🐍 Keep your legs together like a long tail and wiggle your whole body side to side. Slither forward a teeny bit if you can! Flick your tongue and hisss hello.

funFact: Sharks were swimming in the ocean before trees even existed on land!
story: Sherman the shark glided through the waves with his fin poking out of the water — dun dun... dun dun... here comes the friendliest shark in the sea!
description: Start in a plank on your hands and knees, strong shark! 🦈 Roll to one side, stacking your feet or keeping your bottom knee down for a helper. Reach your top arm straight up — that's your fin! Hold steady, then swim to the other side. Dun dun!
safetyNote: Keep your bottom knee on the floor if your arm gets tired. Practice on a mat.

funFact: An octopus has three hearts and can change color like a rainbow!
story: Ozzy the octopus danced in the coral garden, wiggling all eight arms at once while the fish clapped their fins.
description: Sit or stand, wobbly octopus! 🐙 Make all your arms and legs go soft and noodly. Wiggle one arm, then the other, then everything at once — you have eight wiggly tentacles! Now let them float down sloooow and still, like settling on the sea floor.

funFact: Crabs really do walk sideways — their legs bend the perfect way for scuttling!
story: Carlos the crab scuttled sideways across the beach, then froze like a rock whenever a seagull flew over. Tricky crab!
description: Sit down, put your hands behind you and feet in front, snappy crab! 🦀 Press down and lift your bottom off the floor — you're a crab table! Take three sideways crab steps... then FREEZE with your bottom up! Snap snap, well done!

funFact: Bees buzz because their wings beat about two hundred times every second!
story: Bizzy the bee finished visiting one hundred flowers, then sat on a sunny petal humming her favorite honey song.
description: Sit comfy and close your eyes, busy bee. 🐝 Take a big sniff of flower air through your nose. Now breathe out with your lips closed and HUMMMM like a bee — feel the buzz tickle your nose! Try three buzzy breaths. So calming!

funFact: Gorillas are gentle giants — they mostly munch plants and take cozy afternoon naps!
story: Gus the gorilla stood at the top of the hill, gave his chest a proud pat-pat-pat, then sat down gently to share bananas with his family.
description: Stand strong with your feet wide, gentle gorilla! 🦍 Pat your chest softly with open hands — pat-pat-pat-pat! Add a friendly HOO-HOO-HOO! Now FREEZE, standing tall and mighty. You're the kindest, strongest gorilla around.

funFact: Wolves howl to say hello to family far away — it's their long-distance phone call!
story: Willow the wolf pup climbed the moonlit rock, lifted her nose to the stars, and sent a howl all the way home: I'm here, I'm here!
description: Kneel tall or stand strong, brave wolf! 🐺 Take a huge breath and lift your chin to the moon. Now let out a long, wonderful AWOOOOOO! Try a quiet baby howl, then your biggest pack howl. The whole forest hears you!

funFact: Bears can sniff out a snack from miles away — their noses are two thousand times better than ours!
story: Bruno the bear lumbered through the berry patch on all fours, then froze mid-step when he heard a bunny hop by. Statue bear!
description: Put your hands and feet on the floor with your bottom up high, big bear! 🐻 Walk forward on your paws — right hand, left foot, left hand, right foot. Grrr! Now FREEZE like a statue bear! Hold it... then lumber on.

funFact: Cheetahs are the fastest land animals — zero to sixty in three seconds, faster than most cars!
story: Chai the cheetah crouched low in the golden grass, still as a whisper, counting three... two... one... before her lightning dash.
description: Crouch down low with one foot forward and hands on the ground, speedy cheetah! 🐆 Look straight ahead with laser-focus eyes. Stay frozen and ready... hold it... hold it... Now switch feet — no zooming yet, the stillness is your superpower!

funFact: Seals can hold their breath underwater for a whole cartoon episode — over twenty minutes!
story: Sunny the seal flopped onto her favorite warm rock, lifted her chest to the sky, and clapped her flippers for the dancing waves.
description: Lie on your tummy and press up on your hands, happy seal! 🦭 Lift your chest tall and let your legs rest like a tail behind you. Now clap your hands like flippers — arf arf arf! Give a round of applause for YOU!

funFact: A hedgehog has about five thousand spines, and each one is like a tiny bouncy spring!
story: Hazel the hedgehog found a pile of autumn leaves, curled into a perfect prickly ball, and listened to the wind sing.
description: Kneel down and curl forward over your knees, little hedgehog. 🦔 Tuck your head in gently and wrap your arms around your legs or by your sides. Make yourself small, round, and cozy. Breathe soft... your spines are keeping you safe!

funFact: Squirrels plant thousands of trees by accident when they forget where they buried their acorns!
story: Scout the squirrel found the shiniest acorn in the whole park and nibbled it happily, tail twitching with joy.
description: Squat down on your tiptoes or flat feet, quick squirrel! 🐿️ Hold an invisible acorn in your little paws close to your chest. Nibble-nibble-nibble super fast! Now look left, look right — is anyone watching your treasure?

funFact: Dragonflies can fly forward, backward, and sideways — like tiny shimmering helicopters!
story: Dazzle the dragonfly zipped over the pond, then hovered perfectly still above a lily pad, wings sparkling in the sun.
description: Stand on one leg, shimmering dragonfly! 🪰 Lean forward gently and stretch your other leg back behind you. Spread your arms out wide like glassy wings. Hover as still as you can... then zip up and switch sides!

funFact: A ladybug's spots warn birds that it tastes yucky — the spots are its superpower shield!
story: Lulu the ladybug landed on a leaf, rolled onto her back, and wiggled her tiny legs at the sky until a breeze set her right again.
description: Lie on your back and hug your knees, tiny ladybug! 🐞 Now let go and wave your arms and legs gently up at the sky — wiggle wiggle! Rock a little side to side on your round ladybug shell. Roll to one side and pop up to fly away!

funFact: Jellyfish have no brain, no bones, and no heart — they're mostly water, floating like ocean clouds!
story: Jelly the jellyfish drifted through the warm blue sea, letting the gentle current carry her up... and down... and up again.
description: Stand up and go completely soft and floaty, gentle jellyfish. 🪼 Let your arms drift up sloooow like tentacles in the water... then float them down. Sway your whole body with each breath. There's no hurry in the deep blue sea.

funFact: If a starfish loses an arm, it can grow a brand new one — real ocean magic!
story: Stella the starfish stretched all five arms as wide as she could on the sandy sea floor, soaking up the wavy sunshine.
description: Lie on your back and stretch out WIDE, sparkly starfish! ⭐ Reach your arms and legs out to make a giant star shape. Take a big breath and stretch even wider... then let everything melt soft. You're a star — literally!

funFact: The unicorn is the national animal of Scotland — a real country chose a magical creature!
story: Nova the unicorn pranced across the rainbow bridge, her hooves making tiny sparkles with every joyful step.
description: Stand tall and make a magical horn with your hands on your forehead, dazzling unicorn! 🦄 Prance in place with high, fancy knees — one, two, one, two! Toss your sparkly mane side to side. Every step leaves glitter behind you!

funFact: Dragon tales are told in almost every country on Earth — everyone loves a good dragon story!
story: Ember the dragon guarded her mountain with mighty puffs of warm breath that melted the snow and made spring come early.
description: Stand strong with your feet wide and knees bent, mighty dragon! 🐉 Take a giant breath in through your nose and fill your dragon belly. Now whoosh it all out through your mouth — HAAAAH! — like warm dragon fire. Three fiery breaths and you'll feel brand new!

funFact: Every tiger's stripes are one of a kind, just like your fingerprints!
story: Tara the tiger cub stretched one strong leg way back and reached her nose forward, practicing to be the most graceful cat in the jungle.
description: Come to your hands and knees, striped tiger! 🐯 Stretch one leg long behind you and lift it like a swishing tail. Look forward with fierce, kind tiger eyes. Hold steady... then switch legs. Grrreat job!

funFact: A mouse's heart can beat over six hundred times a minute — but yours slows down nicely in this cozy pose!
story: Pip-squeak the mouse tiptoed into her snug nest of soft cotton, tucked in her tiny nose, and felt perfectly safe and warm.
description: Kneel down and sit back on your heels, tiny mouse. 🐭 Fold forward so your forehead rests on the floor and tuck your paws by your sides. Curl up small, small, smaller... Now be so quiet you can hear your own soft breath. Squeak!

funFact: Puppies stretch like this to say let's play — it's called a play bow!
story: Waffles the puppy spotted his best friend across the park, dropped his chest low, wagged his tail high, and bowed: let's play!
description: Start on your hands and knees, stretchy puppy! 🐶 Keep your hips up high over your knees and walk your paws way out front. Melt your chest and chin toward the floor. That's a perfect puppy play bow — wag that happy tail!

funFact: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep so they don't float away from each other!
story: Ollie the otter lay back on the gentle river, held his favorite shiny pebble on his tummy, and floated under the drifting clouds.
description: Lie on your back, easy-breezy otter. 🦦 Fold your hands on your tummy like you're holding a special pebble. Feel your belly float up as you breathe in... and drift down as you breathe out. Float on your cozy river for a while.

funFact: Ducks have waterproof feathers — water rolls right off, like magic raincoats!
story: Dilly the duckling followed her mama across the farmyard, waddle-waddle-waddling in a proud little line to the pond.
description: Squat down low with your hands tucked under your arms like wings, silly duck! 🦆 Take three little waddle steps forward — waddle, waddle, waddle! Now stop and give your best QUACK QUACK! Waddle on, little duckling!

funFact: A chick taps its way out of the egg with a tiny pointy egg-tooth on its beak!
story: Inside a warm speckled egg, little Pippin curled up tight... then tap, tap, CRACK — hello, big bright world!
description: Curl up small on your knees like you're inside an egg, little chick. 🐣 Tap-tap-tap with your beak... the shell is cracking! Now sloooowly stretch up tall, spread your fluffy new wings, and cheep-cheep hello to the world!

funFact: Koalas sleep up to twenty hours a day, hugging their favorite tree the whole time!
story: Kip the koala found the comfiest branch in the whole eucalyptus tree, wrapped it in a big hug, and drifted into a leafy dream.
description: Sit down and hug your knees in close, sleepy koala. 🐨 Squeeze your cozy tree-hug and rest your cheek on your knees. Rock a tiny bit side to side, like a breeze in the branches. Mmm... comfiest koala ever.

funFact: A blue whale's heart is as big as a small car, and its spout can shoot up thirty feet!
story: Wally the whale rose from the deep, took the hugest breath in the ocean, and sent a sparkling fountain into the sky — whooosh!
description: Lie on your back and lift your legs up toward the sky, great big whale! 🐋 Rest your arms by your sides and float in the deep blue. Take a huge whale breath in... and WHOOSH it out like a sparkly spout! Three big spouts, then float on down.

funFact: Horses can sleep standing up thanks to special locking legs!
story: Copper the pony galloped around the sunny paddock, mane flying, then halted perfectly still when the farmer whistled.
description: Stand tall and hold your invisible reins, speedy horse! 🐎 Gallop in place with high hooves — clip-clop-clip-clop! Now pull the reins gently and FREEZE in a strong horse stance, knees bent, steady and still. Neeeigh! Gallop again when you're ready.

funFact: Bats hang upside down to sleep because their feet lock closed without using any muscles!
story: Bruce the little bat found the coziest spot in the cave, flipped upside down, wrapped up in his wings, and watched the world the fun way.
description: Stand with your feet apart, friendly bat! 🦇 Bend your knees a little and fold forward, letting your head and arms hang down. Wrap your arms around your legs like folded wings. Look at the upside-down world... then roll up slowly, bit by bit.
